name: Compensation and benefits planning
one_line: The employer-side instruments that decide what a job is worth and what a round will pay: grade-and-range structures, job evaluation, third-party salary-survey matches, merit and increase-guideline matrices, pay-review round proposals and budget envelopes, bonus and equity plan rules, and benefit plan-design and cost comparisons. Its signature is a grid keyed by a JOB GRADE or a PLAN OPTION rather than by a person, which is the one hr situation the schema's employee-or-cohort default template does not recognise; the round worksheets that do name individuals are the strictest material in the family and are protected before any model path.

proposed_fields.example: Band 6, Grade M3, or job-match code FIN.ANL.03
proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: This row's organizing axis is absent from the hr schema's own proposed vocabulary, which is the clearest evidence that the row is not a restatement of its schema. All four schema proposals are keyed to a person or a population or a process: `workforce_member` is the individual subject of a personnel record, `workforce_unit` is a department, site, or reporting population, `people_cycle` is a bounded process instance, and `personnel_case` is one employee-relations or safety matter. A salary structure, a job-evaluation scorecard, and a survey match table name NO person, NO department, and often no cycle at all - their row key is the graded job. `role` and `job_title` describe what someone does; a grade is the levelling assignment that a pay range attaches to, and two titles routinely share a grade while one title spans two. Without this key the signature artifact of this row has no legal fact and no possible dimension.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Proposed true, and this is the rare hr key that can be one, because a branch named Band 6 discloses no individual. It should never lead: a grade level is meaningless outside the structure version or round it belongs to. It must also not become a one-child collector in a corpus with a single grade.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: A labelled Grade, Band, Level, or Job Code column is a direct observation, but grade vocabularies are employer-specific, are renamed at every restructure, and collide with survey vendors' own codes. Validation would need an employer-specific grade roster that this row is not licensed to invent, so the inferred fact is capped at possible.

proposed_fields.example: 2026 pay review round, FY2026 bonus plan year, or 2027 benefits renewal
proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: Reused verbatim from the hr schema anchor rather than minted; this row does not propose a variant. Recorded here only because this row makes a stronger claim about it than the schema does - see `template.why`. A merit matrix cell reading three-and-a-half percent is uninterpretable without the round, exactly as `00` describes a homework file being meaningless without the course.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: As proposed on the schema anchor. This row argues it should lead for round-bounded material rather than sit third.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: A labelled round or plan-year title is direct; a bare year on a reward document may be the structure's effective date, the survey's data date, the plan year, or the document's creation date, and no generic date rule separates them.

deterministic: a grid whose ROW KEY IS A GRADE, BAND, LEVEL, OR JOB-MATCH CODE and whose columns are pay-range positions - minimum, midpoint, maximum, range spread, midpoint progression - or market percentiles. No employee is named and none is needed. This is the row's signature and no other hr situation produces it: the schema's default deterministic signals all require labelled slots that jointly identify an employee or a cohort, and this grid identifies neither

a guideline matrix whose two axes are a performance rating and a position-in-range or compa-ratio measure and whose cells are increase percentages, accompanied by a round instruction or budget statement. The two-axis rating-by-range shape is the discriminator, not the word merit

a round worksheet carrying, on one row, a current amount, a PROPOSED or NEW amount, and a unit budget envelope or spend-against-allocation total. The proposal-and-envelope columns are the signal; statutory deduction and net-pay columns instead indicate payroll administration

a plan instrument bearing a plan year, an eligible population, a target percentage or grant value keyed to grade, and a payout curve, gate, proration, or leaver rule. This is an operative instrument for a bounded year, not a standing policy
a benefit plan-design comparison keyed by PLAN OPTION with employer and employee contribution split, coverage tier, and projected employer cost. Keyed by option, not by enrolled employee
a job-evaluation or levelling scorecard whose factor scores resolve to a grade for a job title with no incumbent named

a third-party salary-survey submission or result carrying a participant or subscriber code, job-match codes, and percentile columns, together with separate evidence that the holder is the participating employer
needs_llm: whether a grade-and-range table is the holder's own operative structure or a published, market, or cited table reproduced inside a report, a recruitment advert, a vendor deck, or a news article

whether a workbook carrying both a period-cost tab and a range tab is a budget submission or a reward instrument. The deciding structure is whether the grid resolves to an approved period budget line or to a grade ladder
whether a plan-like document is the operative bonus, equity, or benefit instrument for a bounded year or the standing compensation philosophy and pay policy that governs every year
whether an individually addressed statement of pay is a member of an employer-generated batch or the individual's own employment record held in a personal corpus

whether pay-equity workings are a reward-design exercise or a workforce-analytics or statutory reporting product. Both readings are protected and abstention is the correct answer when the evidence does not decide
never_alone: a currency amount beside a job title. Offer letters, job adverts, recruiter emails, consultant quotes, invoices, and CVs all carry exactly that pair, and the offer-letter fixture in this file is the collision it produces
a percentile, P50, P75, median, or quartile column. Market studies, pricing analyses, survey reports, and performance dashboards all carry percentile columns without being reward instruments
the words compensation, reward, salary, pay, bonus, benefits, band, grade, level, benchmark, or total reward alone, in a filename, heading, or directory name

a single employee's salary letter, payslip, offer, bonus letter, or total reward statement merely because an employer issued it. In a personal corpus those are that individual's own employment and payroll records

a budget line labelled salaries, wages, bonus, benefits, or employer on-costs. A period-keyed budget or ledger stays with business planning or finance unless a grade-keyed or round-keyed structure is present

the holder's firm appearing as employer, letterhead, email domain, author, or custodian, which `00` treats as a role perspective rather than an anchor when it says a university name alone should not create a group because the same name can appear as employer, provider, target, venue, or a merely cited organization
source type or extension alone, including spreadsheet, presentation, email, calendar, image, OCR, or archive
a bare year, percentage, currency amount, grade-shaped token such as M3 or L5, or acronym such as STI, LTI, TRS, or FTE
membership in a download session, mailbox folder, or parent directory named Comp, Reward, Pay, Salary, Confidential, or Do Not Forward
absence of EXIF as proof that an image of a range chart or a planning-tool screen is a screenshot

work_types: salary structure, grade ladder, or pay-range table and its effective-dated revisions
job evaluation, levelling, or job-architecture scorecard and its grade outcome
third-party salary-survey submission, job-match mapping, or percentile result set
market positioning or competitiveness analysis against a stated pay policy line
pay-review round instruction, merit or increase-guideline matrix, and budget allocation
manager pay-proposal worksheet, calibration extract, and round approval record
bonus or short-term-incentive plan rules, target schedule, and payout modelling
equity or long-term-incentive grant guideline keyed to grade
benefit plan design, option comparison, renewal broker report, and employer cost model
total reward statement generation batch and its templates and communication pack
pay-equity or pay-gap design workings held to inform structure and round decisions
grouping_reasons: one pay-review round from instruction and matrix through unit proposal worksheets, calibration extracts, budget reconciliation, and approval
one salary structure and its effective-dated revisions, joined through universal version_family rather than through a reward-only field
one benefits renewal cycle across broker report, option comparison, employer cost model, and the decision pack
one plan year's instrument family: plan rules, target schedule, payout model, and the communication pack that explains it
one survey participation: submission file, job-match mapping, and the returned result set, bounded by the survey's own data date
sparse round members such as a lone matrix PDF or a single manager pack may join an accepted round by membership without copying a grade, amount, round, or unit fact onto them

no group is valid when a lone reward-looking file carries only amounts and titles with no grade ladder, round instruction, or plan instrument; protected residual placement is safer than inventing an employer's reward corpus

template.why: Empty because PR-6 leaves the hr schema fieldless and no proposed key may become a folder dimension yet. The prose recommendation held for R1c differs from the schema default in one argued way. The hr default is work type or people programme first, workforce unit second, people cycle third, and never the employee's name. This row's corpus splits in two, which no other hr row's does: STANDING instruments - the grade structure, job evaluations, the survey library - are round-independent and should be ordered work type first, then job grade, with the effective-dated versions carried by version_family; ROUND-BOUNDED instruments - the matrix, the unit worksheets, the budget reconciliation - are uninterpretable outside their round and should put people_cycle FIRST, ahead of work type and unit, on the same reasoning `00` gives when it says a group's members must not carry irreconcilable course, institution, project, term, or purpose facts. Workforce unit may follow the cycle only where several units genuinely submitted; it must not become a one-child collector. A grade may be a leaf-side dimension because it names no person, but it must never lead. The employee's name is never a dimension here even though the round worksheets contain it. Not time-first: an effective date, a data date, a plan year, and a document date are four different things on the same page, so a date cannot define this world.

collides_with.signal: The sharpest collision in the family and the one that could have reduced this row to a lifecycle stage. A pay-round proposal worksheet and a payroll register are both employee-keyed grids of names and salaries. The discriminating evidence is the COLUMN SET, which is testable without knowing any date: proposed increase, new salary, compa-ratio, rating, and a unit budget envelope support this row and describe a decision that has not happened; gross pay, statutory deductions, employer contributions, net pay, and a pay-period control total support payroll administration and describe a transaction that has. The same reciprocal test applies to benefits: a plan-option comparison keyed by option is this row, an enrolment or contribution file keyed by employee is administration. Provenance: inference.

Both rows are grade-aware and neither is person-keyed, so grade cannot decide. The discriminating evidence is what hangs off the grade: pay ranges, market percentiles, increase guidelines, and plan targets support this row; approved posts, vacancies, FTE, reporting lines, and structural moves support org design. One establishment plan that adds a cost column per post is the shared fixture; where the cost is an unpriced budget assumption it stays with org design, and where it is derived from the range table it crosses here. Provenance: inference.

Pay-gap and pay-distribution workings are the shared fixture and both readings are defensible. The discriminating evidence is the intended use visible in the file: workings held against a named structure version or round, produced to move ranges or set a budget, support this row; a population measurement series with period-over-period cuts and a reporting output supports analytics. Neither reading changes the protection, and where the file does not decide, abstention is correct. Provenance: inference.

The holder-role seam, and the one that produces this row's collision fixture. An offer letter, a salary-change letter, a bonus letter, and a total reward statement carry a grade, a salary, and a bonus target - every token this row recognises - but they are instruments addressed to ONE individual. The discriminating evidence: an individually addressed instrument in a personal corpus is the individual's own employment record; the same bytes are this row's evidence only as a member of an employer-held generation batch or template set with a round or plan-year anchor. Provenance: inference.

Reciprocal to the edge that row already authored against this one, and named on the same fixture: the people cost model. That row states that roles, FTE counts and aggregate cost with no names support it, while named individuals, salary bands, or personal review outcomes support this row, and that a single spreadsheet frequently crosses at one column, where the stricter side wins. This side adds the test that does not depend on names: period columns resolving to a submitted-and-approved budget line support budget-forecast; grade rows with range or market columns, or a rating-by-range guideline matrix, support this row. Provenance: inference.

A compensation philosophy and a bonus plan document are both policy-shaped. The discriminating evidence: a version-control table, an owner, an approval and next-review date, and handbook numbering support the handbook; a plan year, an eligible population, targets keyed to grade, and a payout curve support this row because they are an operative instrument for one bounded cycle rather than a standing rule. The hr schema anchor already draws this seam family-wide; the plan-year test is this row's specific contribution to it. Provenance: inference.

An equity grant guideline table keyed to grade and an actual grant record are the shared fixture. The discriminating evidence: grant VALUE bands keyed to grade with no grantee support this row as a reward design instrument; grantee identity, share counts, strike price, vesting schedules, and instrument identifiers support cap-table equity as an ownership record. A guideline that has been populated with grantees has crossed, and the ownership reading wins. Provenance: inference.

also_holds_with.signal: The benefits renewal fixture legitimately carries both readings at once rather than confusing them. A group medical, life, or income-protection plan-design comparison is simultaneously an employer reward instrument and a corporate insurance record: the option, insurer, coverage tier, and premium structure are insurance facts, while the employer-versus-employee contribution split and the projected employer cost are reward-design facts. Neither reading should erase the other, and neither may manufacture a clinical fact about any person. Provenance: inference.

sensitivity_why: This row inverts the schema's privacy logic, which is the third leg of its node test. The hr default protects material BECAUSE it identifies a person; here the least personal files are among the most sensitive. A grade-and-range table, a merit matrix, and a survey result set name nobody and are still restricted: they expose pay-equity position, negotiation posture, and licensed third-party data whose redistribution terms sit on the file itself. The round worksheets are strict for the ordinary reason as well, since they carry a named individual's current salary, rating, and proposed increase together - a combination no payslip and no review form produces on its own. The practical rule is that the absence of names must not be read as a reason to relax handling, that pay-round and pay-gap material should be recognised locally from labels and headers rather than sent as a dossier, and that no branch label should expose an individual's pay position. This node records only `potentially_sensitive`; P7 owns handling classes.
open_question: Three items are unresolved and are argued in the memo: whether `job_grade` is minted at all or whether R1c folds grade into the existing `workforce_unit` proposal (this row argues it must not); whether the pay-gap fixture is a collision with `hr.workforce-analytics` or a co-holding within one schema, which CONNECTION's `also_holds_with` does not clearly cover for same-schema siblings; and whether a remuneration-committee pack should carry an edge to this row, which `business_operations.board-governance` deliberately refused and this row deliberately does not author back.
